title: component-audit-prioritization-and-assistive-flow-notes-2026-10
body:
Intent and context
- Quick working doc for triaging component-level accessibility and UX risk across the console. Focus is practical: fixes that unblock feature launches (rollouts, model selection flows, cost breakdowns) and low-effort wins for keyboard and screen reader users.
- Not a full WCAG audit; this is component-first and implementation-aware. Will feed into CON-898 and the sprint grooming session.

Summary of outcomes sought
- Prioritized list of components to update in v1.3 (release target: 2026-11).
- Concrete assistive-flow notes for three high-impact pages: Deploy modal, Rollout editor, Model catalog list.
- Acceptance criteria and rough effort estimates to triage into backlog.

High-level observations from quick-pass review (Oct 2-4)
- Many components visually conform to color tokens but lack consistent ARIA labels and semantics when used in compound patterns (lists + actions).
- Virtualized lists (model catalog) break expected focus order when inline actions open dialogs. Keyboard users lose context.
- Toast/alert announcements for streaming logs and generation state are noisy for screen readers; need polite vs assertive mapping.
- Contrast is generally OK in tokens, but certain overlay states and disabled variants drop below 3:1 for body-large labels.

Prioritization matrix (rationale, not a spreadsheet)
- P1 (High impact, low-medium effort):
  - Virtualized list focus trap when action opens inline drawer on model card (affects sign-up funnel and model switching). Rationale: blocks keyboard users from finishing model switch flows; straightforward fix by moving focus into drawer and restoring.
  - Toast announcement semantics for streaming generation: currently assertive for each partial update; change to polite with a final assertive on completion for errors. Rationale: immediate user benefit in chat/streaming experiences; small code change in notification manager.
  - Form input labels in Deploy modal: some dynamic fields are missing explicit aria-labelledby when toggled by feature flag. Rationale: high impact for customers configuring private deployments; quick review + automated test.
- P2 (Medium impact, medium effort):
  - Action menus inside table rows (cost breakdown table) lose accessible name computation when icons used without fallback text. Rationale: medium frequency, fix requires component API alignment.
  - Color token variant for disabled chips inside tag filters falls below contrast ratio in dark mode. Rationale: visual regression risk; requires design token update and visual regression testing.
- P3 (Low immediate impact / higher effort):
  - Revisit modal stacking semantics across console routes to ensure aria-hidden on background content for nested modals. Rationale: edge case for embedded SSO flows; larger refactor.

Assistive-flow notes (deploy modal)
- Entry point: keyboard focus lands on primary trigger button (Deploy). When activated:
  - Move focus to modal heading element (role dialog with aria-modal). Provide aria-describedby referencing short summary lines for current config.
  - All dynamic toggles must update aria-expanded and aria-controls. When a toggle reveals additional fields, ensure the first revealed field receives programmatic focus only for keyboard contexts; otherwise announce via aria-live polite region.
  - Save/Confirm action: on success, do not navigate away automatically. Instead announce via aria-live polite with summary text and leave focus on success banner with an actionable link to view rollout. Screen reader should hear: deployment successful, view rollout. Make the link tabbable.
Acceptance criteria (deploy modal)
- Keyboard: tab order traverses from heading -> close button -> first interactive -> final action -> success link.
- Screen reader: correct modal semantics, aria-describedby present, no duplicate announcements during toggles.
- Tests: add a11y e2e in Storybook using axe-core and keyboard focus test for modal.
Estimated effort: 2-3 dev days + 1 design day.

Assistive-flow notes (rollout editor)
- Problem: rollout percentage slider is not keyboard operable with fine-grain adjustments; tooltip announcements are visual-only.
- Recommendation: add keyboard step handlers (arrow keys +/- 1%, PageUp/PageDown +/-10%) and an aria-valuetext that verbalizes percent and target cohort name. When changing value, update a polite aria-live region that reads: rollout target now X percent for cohort Y.
- Edge case: when auto-fallback is enabled, toggling it should immediately announce status change as assertive only on failure.
Acceptance criteria (rollout editor)
- Slider operable by keyboard and announces value changes.
- Screen reader user can understand fallback state and can trigger immediate rollback via keyboard-only interactions.
Estimated effort: 3-4 dev days + 1 QA day.

Assistive-flow notes (model catalog list, virtualized)
- Symptoms observed: keyboard users tab into list, navigate to item, open inline details (drawer) but focus remains on list container; arrow keys continue to virtualize and skip items.
- Quick fix: when opening inline details, toggle a class that pauses virtualization for visible window and set inert attribute on list behind the drawer. Move focus to drawer heading. On close, restore previous scroll/focus.
- Longer-term: consider exposing roving tabindex on virtualized rows to preserve predictable focus.
Acceptance criteria (catalog)
- Drawer open puts focus into drawer and traps it; closing restores prior focus spot.
- No skipping of items when user uses arrow keys to navigate within opened context.
Estimated effort: quick fix 2 dev days; longer refactor 1 week.

Component-level notes and small fixes (short task list)
- Button icon-only components: ensure aria-label required at type level; update lint rule in eslint-plugin to error on missing label. (DEV-frontend-184)
- Tag chip keyboard focus styles: visible focus ring inconsistent across density variants; update focus token usage and add story variant. (design + 1 dev day)
- Status badges: add role=status for live status inside streaming panels; ensure aria-live polite on repeated updates and assertive only on error.
- Table row action overflow: add accessible name on menu triggers; fix computeAccessibleName in table-cell component.

Backlog grooming notes (to split into Jira)
- CON-898: Deploy modal a11y fixes (split into 4 sub-tasks: focus, labeling, live regions, tests)
- CON-899: Virtualized list drawer focus trap and inert toggle
- CON-900: Streaming notifications behavior change and tests
- CON-901: Slider keyboard semantics and aria-valuetext updates
- Spike item: quantify performance trade-offs for pausing virtualization (link to infra ticket INF-1221). Assign to Julian for initial exploration.

Open questions and unresolved trade-offs
- How aggressive should we be with aria-live politeness for streaming partial updates in different product tiers? (hosted chat vs dedicated internal tooling). Need product decision.
- Is pausing virtualization acceptable for large catalogs (1000+ models) from a perf standpoint? Spike required.
- Should we standardize on inert vs aria-hidden for background content when modals are open? Some older browsers lack inert support; polyfills may be needed.

Next steps and owners
- Assign CON-898 sub-tasks in grooming meeting (Oct 13). Owner for modal focus: Sana. Owner for live regions: Tomoko.
- Julian to run virtualization spike by Oct 20 and report perf metrics to infra.
- Add a11y e2e stories for Deploy modal, Rollout editor, and Model catalog in Storybook. Add checklist to PR template for accessible name, focus trap, and contrast token check.

Notes to self (raw)
- look at previous focus management patterns in sso-embed modal (was done in 2025, might reuse code).
- confirm color token names for disabled-chip-secondary in dark mode with design tokens doc.
- run a quick axe scan on staging after fixes and capture failures for CON-900.

End of doc
